changelog.summary: Leave pay rules: pay kept for sick days is the employer's payment for the first two working days (KSO art. 40(5)), insured but not taxed (ZDDFL art. 24(2)(14)); before, it was taxed. Sick pay on more days than two working days can span is refused (a top-up is taxable and not separated).
2026 rates and limits, including the 1 August 2026 changes to the maximum insurable income, the minimum insurable income (annex 1A) and the work-accident rates (annex 2A).

steps.message: Labour categories I and II (professional pension fund) are not supported by this template
The ZDDFL art. 18 disability relief is not supported by this template
Pre-tax deductions are not supported by this template: the ZDDFL art. 19 reliefs on the monthly tax base are not modelled
Bulgarian contributions are monthly: the pay period must be a whole calendar month

Sick pay on more days than the first two working days of an absence is not supported: the employer's payment under KSO art. 40(5) covers the first two working days and is not taxed (ZDDFL art. 24(2)(14)), while pay beyond it is taxable wage the template does not separate
The employee's statutory profile needs qualificationGroup (NKPD group 1–9), or a minimumInsurableIncome

Remuneration is below the full-month minimum insurable income in a partial month (or part-time, unpaid or sick leave). The minimum is prorated by the days worked and the employer's sick days (KSO art. 40(5)) over Bulgaria's working days; set the prorated amount as the employee's minimumInsurableIncome

steps.label: Pension fund (DOO, in place of the universal fund)

limitations: Monthly payroll calendars whose periods are whole calendar months, paid in EUR.
Labour category III only; categories I and II (professional pension fund) are refused.

Partial months, part-time work, unpaid or sick leave with pay below the full-month minimum insurable income need a prorated minimumInsurableIncome (days worked and the employer's sick days, NEVDVPOV art. 1): working days come from Bulgaria's official calendar, which Humano does not hold.

Leave pay rules: pay kept for sick days is taken as the employer's payment for the first two working days (KSO art. 40(5): 70% of the month's average daily gross pay), insured but not taxed (ZDDFL art. 24(2)(14)); sick pay on more than four calendar days in a month is refused, and an employer top-up above the statutory 70% is not separated. From the third day the National Social Security Institute pays outside payroll. No statutory leave pay rule is declared: the law counts working days, leave pay rules count calendar days of the absence.
Occupation-specific annex rows (e.g. hospital nurses, professional footballers) need the employee's minimumInsurableIncome.
One payroll run per month: remuneration from other runs in the same month is not added before applying the maximum insurable income.
Monthly tax-base reliefs (ZDDFL art. 18 disability, art. 19 voluntary insurance) and the annual tax recalculation are not applied; employees with tenant pre-tax deductions are refused.
Remuneration for work in past months (KSO art. 6(2) redistribution) is treated as current-month income.
Each contribution and the tax are rounded to the cent, half up, line by line; this is common practice but not cited to a legal provision.
Status LAW_DERIVED: every value is cited to the law; no official worked example was found to compare the results against.
